$comment: The register from docs/clinical-scope-boundary.md §3, as data. The model and the deterministic detector read THIS FILE so they cannot drift apart. Amending this file is a clinical act: it requires the sign-off named in clinician_of_record. Not yet signed off — see docs/clinical-scope-boundary.md §8.

B.route: contact clinic today; urgent care or ED if unreachable
B.basis: IFOMPT emergency referral: 'as a guide, on the same day' [6]

C.basis: IFOMPT urgent referral: 'as a guide, within 5 days' [6]
C.open_question: Should this tier stop the intake instead? See §8.1.

flags.reported: Chest discomfort lasting more than a few minutes or coming and going; discomfort in one or both arms, back, shoulders, neck, jaw or upper stomach; shortness of breath; cold sweat, nausea, lightheadedness

Sudden numbness or weakness of face, arm or leg especially one side; sudden confusion or trouble speaking; sudden trouble seeing; sudden difficulty walking, dizziness or loss of balance; sudden severe headache with no known cause

Neck or head pain WITH any of: unsteadiness or ataxia, slurred or disturbed speech, difficulty swallowing, facial droop, drooping eyelid, double vision or visual disturbance, facial numbness, nausea and vomiting, loss of consciousness
flags.note: Framework percentages inform WHICH items are listed, never a weighting — the framework states they are 'not intended to inform any judgement on relative risk'.

flags.reported: Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain together with calf pain or swelling
New numbness in the buttocks, inner thighs or genitals, including loss of normal sensation when wiping after toileting
flags.source: IFOMPT spinal framework, CES cue card [6]

flags.reported: New difficulty passing urine, incomplete emptying, hesitancy, not feeling the bladder fill, or incontinence
flags.source: IFOMPT spinal framework, CES cue card [6]

flags.reported: New bowel incontinence or inability to control the bowels
flags.source: IFOMPT spinal framework, CES cue card [6]

flags.reported: New sexual dysfunction alongside back or leg symptoms
flags.source: IFOMPT spinal framework, CES cue card [6]

flags.reported: Leg pain that began on one side and is now both sides, or alternates sides, with new weakness
flags.source: IFOMPT: presentations increasing probability of acute threatened CES [6]

flags.reported: Leg weakness that is getting worse, or new trouble walking
flags.source: IFOMPT: abnormal and progressing neurological deficit [6]

flags.reported: Calf or leg pain with swelling, warmth, redness or discoloration
flags.source: APTA VTE CPG 2022 key action statement [10]
flags.note: The agent does NOT apply Wells criteria. The guideline assigns that to the therapist.

flags.reported: History of cancer with new spinal pain, particularly thoracic
Night pain where they cannot get back to sleep — walking the floors, sitting in a chair, lying on the floor with minimal relief
Unexplained weight loss, or feeling systemically unwell — fatigue, nausea, loss of appetite
Band-like pain around the trunk
flags.source: IFOMPT: may indicate metastatic spinal cord compression [6]

flags.reported: Fever or chills with spinal pain
flags.source: IFOMPT infection: classic triad is back pain, fever, neurological dysfunction; absence of fever cannot rule out [6]

flags.reported: Immunosuppression (diabetes, HIV, rheumatoid arthritis, long-term steroids, heavy alcohol use), recent infection, recent spinal or abdominal surgery, or intravenous drug use, with new spinal pain
Known osteoporosis, previous fragility fracture, or steroid tablets/inhalers over months, with new spinal pain
Recent fall, trauma or lifting event followed by pain unlike their usual pain
Anything indicating thoughts of suicide or self-harm
flags.note: No risk assessment. No follow-up questions. The number, and stop.

excluded_by_design.reason: Requires examination by a suitably trained clinician (IFOMPT sign tables [6]). If a trigger cannot be phrased as a sentence a patient would say about themselves, it does not belong in this system.
